question: What is the main goal of postnatal care provided by a midwife right inside the family's home?

options.A: Providing routine cooking lessons for the new family
options.B: Delivering professional midwifery services inside the family home
options.C: Replacing all hospital checkups with television consultations
options.D: Conducting mandatory immunization drives at local schools

explanation: Domiciliary care means taking clinical assessment and support directly to where the mother and baby live after birth. [learn more](BMP215_U2_T4#BMP215_U2_T4_h1)

question: Why are home visits important when a mother leaves the hospital very early after birth?

options.A: They force the family to purchase extra hospital equipment
options.B: They allow the midwife to permanently reside with the family
options.C: They guarantee that the baby will never catch any childhood illness
options.D: They bridge the gap to ensure continuity of care after leaving the facility

explanation: Early discharge can leave mothers vulnerable before complications fully show, making home visits essential for ongoing monitoring. [learn more](BMP215_U2_T4#BMP215_U2_T4_h1)

question: When should the very first postnatal home visit happen after birth or hospital discharge?

options.A: Exactly at the end of the sixth week
options.B: Between the third and fourth month
options.C: Only when the infant starts teething

explanation: The first visit happens early to catch acute issues like heavy bleeding or feeding difficulties right away. [learn more](BMP215_U2_T4#BMP215_U2_T4_h2)

question: What is a main focus during the postnatal home visit around days three to five?

options.B: Screening for neonatal jaundice and milk transition
options.C: Fitting the mother for permanent surgical sterilization
options.D: Assessing the baby for first tooth eruption

explanation: Days three to five mark when breast milk comes in fully and neonatal jaundice becomes most visible. [learn more](BMP215_U2_T4#BMP215_U2_T4_h2)

question: What does a firm, midline uterus feel like during an abdominal check?
explanation: A firm and centrally located uterus shows that the muscular organ is contracting down properly after birth. [learn more](BMP215_U2_T4#BMP215_U2_T4_h3)

question: What does a foul-smelling lochia discharge during a home visit usually suggest?

options.A: Rapid increase in breast milk production
options.B: Successful healing of an episiotomy wound
options.D: A uterine or genital tract infection

explanation: Foul-smelling lochia is an abnormal finding that points toward postpartum infection requiring medical treatment. [learn more](BMP215_U2_T4#BMP215_U2_T4_h3)

question: Which sign around the umbilical cord stump points to an infection called omphalitis?

options.A: Complete drying up and natural falling off
options.B: A clear droplet of normal tissue fluid
options.C: Redness spreading onto the abdominal skin
options.D: Slight darkening of the cord tissue color

explanation: Spreading redness around the base of the cord indicates bacterial infection, requiring prompt care. [learn more](BMP215_U2_T4#BMP215_U2_T4_h4)

question: Why is checking the baby's body temperature a high priority during early home visits?

options.A: High temperature proves the baby is exclusively breastfed
options.B: It is the only way to predict the adult height of the child
options.C: Newborns struggle to regulate heat and can easily develop hypothermia or fever
options.D: Normal room temperature makes infant checks unnecessary

explanation: Babies lose heat rapidly and lack mature temperature control, making thermal stability a key marker of health. [learn more](BMP215_U2_T4#BMP215_U2_T4_h4)

question: Which observation shows that a baby has a correct and effective breastfeeding latch?

options.A: The infant only sucking gently on the tip of the nipple
options.B: More areola visible above the baby's top lip than below
options.C: The baby making clicking noises with deep dimpled cheeks
options.D: The mother feeling sharp, pinching pain throughout the feed

explanation: An asymmetrical latch places more breast tissue in the infant's lower mouth, ensuring effective milk transfer without nipple trauma. [learn more](BMP215_U2_T4#BMP215_U2_T4_h5)

question: How can a midwife check if a solely breastfed newborn is getting enough milk?

options.A: By weighing the mother before and after each feeding session
options.B: By checking the frequency of wet diapers and infant weight gain
options.C: By testing the protein content of the mother's casual sweat
options.D: By measuring the exact duration of the baby's afternoon nap

explanation: Adequate urine output and steady weight gain are reliable clinical proof that the baby is taking in enough milk. [learn more](BMP215_U2_T4#BMP215_U2_T4_h5)

question: Which of these is a danger sign in a postpartum mother that needs immediate attention?

options.A: Experiencing mild afterpains during infant breastfeeding
options.B: Soaking more than one large sanitary pad per hour
options.C: Feeling slightly tired during the first week at home
options.D: Gradual lightening of lochia color from red to pink

explanation: Heavy bleeding that soaks a large pad every hour indicates postpartum hemorrhage and requires emergency action. [learn more](BMP215_U2_T4#BMP215_U2_T4_h6)

question: What does it mean when jaundice spreads down to the baby's palms and soles?

options.A: A harmless reaction to normal room lighting in the house
options.B: A severe level of bilirubin that requires urgent medical attention
options.C: An indication that the baby is drinking too much clean water
options.D: A normal skin pigmentation change common in breastfed infants

explanation: When jaundice spreads to the extremities like palms and soles, it points to high bilirubin levels needing phototherapy. [learn more](BMP215_U2_T4#BMP215_U2_T4_h6)

question: Where should the midwife record all findings and advice given during a home visit?

options.A: On a personal notebook kept at the midwife's home
options.B: In the mother-infant home-based record booklet
options.C: Inside a private social media group chat online
options.D: Only on the wall calendar inside the family kitchen

explanation: Official home-based records stay with the family and ensure every healthcare worker sees past treatments and assessments. [learn more](BMP215_U2_T4#BMP215_U2_T4_h7)

question: What is the main goal of setting up clear community referral pathways during home care?

options.A: Allowing families to bypass medical personnel during emergencies
options.B: Ensuring fast and safe transfer of complicated cases to a higher health facility
options.C: Reducing the paperwork burden on community health volunteers
options.D: Permanently stopping patients from visiting government hospitals

explanation: Referral pathways connect home care seamlessly to emergency medical services when complications arise. [learn more](BMP215_U2_T4#BMP215_U2_T4_h7)
